socfpga_timer.h

Timer hardware abstraction driver interface for the SoCFPGA bare-metal software stack.

Constants
TIMER_NUM_INSTANCE

Defines the maximum number of hardware timer instances available on the SoCFPGA platform (typically combinations of System Timers and SP Timers).

Types
timer_handle_t

An opaque software handle representing an active connection to a specific hardware timer instance. This handle encapsulates the internal state, including the computed MMIO base address, current clock frequency, and registered interrupt service routines.

timer_callback_t

Callback function signature used by the Timer's Interrupt Service Routine (ISR).  This is executed when the timer hardware reaches zero (in user-defined mode) or rolls over (in free-running mode), triggering a hardware interrupt.

Parameters
buf

An opaque pointer provided by the application during callback registration, typically used to pass application context back to the interrupt handler.

timer_instance_t

Enumerates the physical timer instances available on the SoCFPGA system.

Values
TIMER_SYS0

System Timer 0. Often used for OS ticks or global timekeeping.

TIMER_SYS1

System Timer 1.

TIMER_SP0

SP (System Peripheral) Timer 0. General-purpose timer.

TIMER_SP1

SP (System Peripheral) Timer 1. General-purpose timer.

TIMER_N_INSTANCE

The total number of addressable timer instances.

timer_drv_hw_open
timer_handle_t timer_drv_hw_open(
timer_instance_t 
instance
)

Initializes the hardware mapping for a specific timer instance. It resolves the MMIO base address, interfaces with the System Manager to ensure the peripheral clock is ungated, and asserts/deasserts the hardware reset line via the Reset Manager to ensure a clean operational state.

Parameters
instance
timer_instance_t

The physical hardware identifier from timer_instance_t.

Returns

A valid timer_handle_t on success; NULL if the instance is invalid, already in use, or the hardware clock fails to enable.

timer_ll_open
timer_handle_t timer_ll_open(
timer_instance_t 
instance
)

Allocates and initializes the software context required to manage the timer.  This functions similarly to timer_drv_hw_open but is specifically tailored for the low-level abstraction layer, setting up internal descriptors before hardware configuration begins.

Parameters
instance
timer_instance_t

The physical hardware identifier from timer_instance_t.

Returns

A valid timer_handle_t on success; NULL on failure.

timer_get_value_raw
int32_t timer_get_value_raw(
timer_handle_t const 
htimer,
uint32_t 
*
counter_val
)

Performs a direct read of the hardware's Current Value Register (CVR).  This returns the exact number of clock ticks remaining before the timer hits zero or rolls over, without any software-level conversion.

Parameters
htimer
timer_handle_t const

The active timer handle.

counter_val
uint32_t*

Pointer to a 32-bit variable where the raw hardware tick count will be stored.

Returns

0 on success.  -EINVAL if the handle or pointer is NULL.  -EPERM if the timer is currently stopped and the register is inactive.

timer_ll_start
int32_t timer_ll_start(
timer_handle_t const 
htimer
)

Asserts the Enable bit in the timer's Control Register. This unmasks the timer's output line, allowing it to begin actively decrementing the value loaded from the Load Count Register on every peripheral clock edge.

Parameters
htimer
timer_handle_t const

The active timer handle to start.

Returns

0 on success.  -EINVAL if the handle is NULL.  -EBUSY if the timer is already running.

timer_ll_stop
int32_t timer_ll_stop(
timer_handle_t const 
htimer
)

Clears the Enable bit in the timer's Control Register. This instantly halts the hardware counter and masks its interrupt output to the system's Generic Interrupt Controller (GIC), effectively pausing the timer.

Parameters
htimer
timer_handle_t const

The active timer handle to stop.

Returns

0 on success.  -EINVAL if the handle is NULL.  -EPERM if the timer is already stopped.  -EFAULT if the driver fails to mask the hardware interrupt.

timer_ll_close
int32_t timer_ll_close(
timer_handle_t const 
htimer
)

Safely deconstructs the software context for a timer. It stops the hardware counter (if running), clears pending interrupts, unregisters the ISR, and frees the handle memory.

Parameters
htimer
timer_handle_t const

The active timer handle to close.

Returns

0 on success; -EINVAL if the handle is NULL.

timer_set_period_us
int32_t timer_set_period_us(
timer_handle_t const 
htimer,
uint32_t 
period
)

Configures the timer's operational mode and duration. The driver calculates the required hardware ticks by factoring the requested microseconds against the SoC's active peripheral clock rate, and writes this value into the Load Count Register.

If a finite period is requested, the timer operates in User-Defined (Auto-Reload) Mode, meaning it will automatically reload the count and fire an interrupt every time it hits zero. If the requested period is 0xFFFFFFFF, the timer is configured in Free-Running Mode, utilizing its maximum 32-bit span.

Parameters
htimer
timer_handle_t const

The active timer handle.

period
uint32_t

The desired period in microseconds. (Pass 0xFFFFFFFF for free-running).

Returns

0 on success.  -EINVAL if the handle is NULL or the requested period exceeds the 32-bit hardware limit.  -EBUSY if the timer is currently running and must be stopped before reconfiguration.

timer_get_value_us
int32_t timer_get_value_us(
timer_handle_t const 
htimer,
uint32_t 
*
time_us
)

Reads the hardware's Current Value Register (CVR) and converts the raw tick count back into a human-readable microsecond format. In User-Defined mode, this represents the time remaining until the next interrupt fires. In Free-Running mode, this represents the time until a 32-bit rollover occurs.

Parameters
htimer
timer_handle_t const

The active timer handle.

time_us
uint32_t*

Pointer to a variable where the remaining time in microseconds will be stored.

Returns

0 on success.  -EINVAL if the handle or output pointer is NULL.  -EPERM if the timer is stopped.

timer_set_callback
int32_t timer_set_callback(
timer_handle_t const 
htimer,
timer_callback_t 
callback,
void 
*
param
)

Registers a user-defined function to be executed by the Interrupt Service Routine (ISR) when the hardware timer reaches zero. In auto-reload mode, this callback will be triggered periodically.

Parameters
htimer
timer_handle_t const

The active timer handle.

callback
timer_callback_t

The function pointer to invoke upon timer expiry.

param
void*

An opaque pointer to user context that will be passed directly to the callback function.

Returns

0 on success; -EINVAL if the handle or callback pointer is NULL.
